PM Kisan Yojana 2026

Last updated: 2026-09-15

PM Kisan Samman Nidhi is a central government scheme that provides ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments to eligible farmer families across India. The amount is transferred directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts.

S
Samjho Content Team
Finance and policy experts with 5+ years of experience helping Indians understand money, documents and government schemes.

Simple explanation

PM Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana was launched by the Government of India to provide income support to all land-holding farmer families across the country. Under this scheme, eligible farmer families receive ₹6,000 per year, paid in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 each, typically every four months.

The scheme covers all farmer families regardless of the size of their landholding, subject to certain exclusion criteria. The financial benefit is intended to help farmers meet expenses related to agriculture and allied activities, as well as domestic needs.

The amount is transferred directly to the beneficiary's bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). This ensures transparency and reduces the possibility of delays or intermediaries. Farmers must ensure their bank account details and Aadhaar are correctly linked to receive payments.

As of 2025, the scheme continues to be one of the largest direct benefit transfer programmes for farmers in India. Eligibility, instalment schedules and application processes are governed by official guidelines issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

Why does it matter?

For millions of small and marginal farmers in India, PM Kisan provides a predictable source of income support that can help with seeds, fertilizers, equipment and household expenses. Understanding eligibility and application procedures helps farmers access benefits they are entitled to, and avoid common mistakes that can delay or block payments.

Example

In numbers

Consider a farmer family in Uttar Pradesh owning 2 acres of agricultural land. If they meet the eligibility criteria and complete the registration with correct bank and Aadhaar details, they would receive ₹2,000 in the first instalment (typically April–July), ₹2,000 in the second instalment (August–November), and ₹2,000 in the third instalment (December–March), totaling ₹6,000 for the year. The exact instalment periods are notified by the government and may vary slightly year to year.

Important things to know

  • The scheme provides ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 each to eligible farmer families.
  • All land-holding farmer families are potentially eligible, subject to specific exclusion criteria defined by the government.
  • Certain categories are excluded, such as institutional landholders, former and present ministers, MPs, MLAs, mayors, and income tax payers, among others.
  • Registration requires correct bank account details, Aadhaar linkage, and land ownership records as per state/UT norms.
  • Payments are made through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly to the beneficiary's bank account.
  • Farmers can check their payment status and registration details through the official PM Kisan portal (pmkisan.gov.in).
  • The scheme is fully funded by the Government of India.
  • Always verify current eligibility criteria and instalment schedules from official government sources, as guidelines may be updated.

Common mistakes

  • Not linking Aadhaar with the bank account, which can delay or block DBT payments.
  • Providing incorrect bank account details during registration, leading to failed transfers.
  • Assuming eligibility without checking the exclusion criteria — some categories of landholders are not eligible.
  • Not updating land records or personal details when changes occur, which can affect future instalments.
  • Relying on unofficial sources or agents for application — the official portal is pmkisan.gov.in and registration is free.
  • Missing the self-declaration or e-KYC requirements that may be mandated for continued benefits.

Frequently asked questions

Who is eligible for PM Kisan Samman Nidhi?

All land-holding farmer families across India are potentially eligible, subject to exclusion criteria. Excluded categories typically include institutional landholders, former and present ministers, MPs, MLAs, mayors, members of local bodies, serving or retired government employees with monthly pension above a specified threshold, professionals like doctors and engineers, and income tax payers. Always check the latest official guidelines for the complete and current list.

How much money do farmers receive under PM Kisan?

Eligible farmer families receive ₹6,000 per year, paid in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 each. The instalments are typically transferred every four months, though exact dates are notified by the government.

How can I check my PM Kisan payment status?

You can check your payment status on the official PM Kisan portal at pmkisan.gov.in using your registration number, mobile number, or Aadhaar number. The portal shows instalment history and current status.

How do I apply for PM Kisan Samman Nidhi?

New farmers can apply through the official PM Kisan portal (pmkisan.gov.in) or through Common Service Centres (CSCs). The application requires land ownership details, bank account information, and Aadhaar. Registration is free — do not pay any agent or intermediary.

What documents are needed for PM Kisan registration?

Typically required documents include proof of land ownership or possession (as per state/UT norms), Aadhaar card, bank account details with passbook or cancelled cheque, and mobile number for OTP verification. Exact document requirements may vary by state.

Is PM Kisan available to tenant farmers or sharecroppers?

Eligibility for tenant farmers and sharecroppers depends on state/UT-specific guidelines and whether they can provide acceptable proof of cultivation. Some states have mechanisms to include them, but this varies. Check with your state agriculture department or the official PM Kisan portal for current rules.

What should I do if my PM Kisan payment is not received?

First, check your status on pmkisan.gov.in to see if the instalment was credited. If the status shows success but money is not in your account, verify your bank account details and Aadhaar linkage. If there's a discrepancy, contact your state nodal officer or use the grievance mechanism on the official portal.

Can I receive PM Kisan benefits if I am an income tax payer?

No. As per the scheme guidelines, income tax payers are generally excluded from PM Kisan benefits. This is one of the key exclusion criteria. If your tax status changes, you should update your details accordingly.
